trivia.a: HyperText Transfer Protocol — the rulebook your browser uses to fetch web pages.

trivia.q: Which company first shipped a commercial computer mouse?
trivia.a: Apple, with the 1984 Macintosh (though the mouse was invented at Xerox PARC in the 1970s).

trivia.q: What does 'RAM' stand for, and why is it called that?
trivia.a: Random Access Memory — any byte can be reached in roughly the same time, unlike tape you'd fast-forward.

trivia.q: What's the difference between HTTPS and HTTP?
trivia.a: The 'S' means secure: the connection is encrypted (TLS), so nobody on the Wi-Fi can read what you send.

trivia.q: Roughly how many characters can a 7-bit ASCII code encode?
trivia.a: 128 — enough for English letters, digits, and basic punctuation.
Graphics Processing Unit — built to crunch many simple math ops at once, which is also why it powers AI.

trivia.q: What year was the first Raspberry Pi released?
trivia.a: 2012 — it kicked off the modern maker and retro-computing boom.

trivia.q: What does 'SSD' stand for, and how is it different from an HDD?
trivia.a: Solid-State Drive. No moving parts, so it's far faster and more shock-proof than a spinning Hard Disk Drive.
A fake message that pretends to be your bank or boss to trick you into handing over passwords or money.
The source code is public and free to use, modify, and share — like Linux.

trivia.q: What is the difference between a modem and a router?
trivia.a: A modem brings the internet in from your provider; a router shares that connection with your devices.
Basic Input/Output System — the firmware that starts your hardware and hands off to the OS.
A fatal error where the OS core can't recover, so the system halts (the Mac's version of a Blue Screen).

trivia.q: How many bits are in a byte?
trivia.a: 8. A byte is the standard unit for one character of text.

trivia.q: What does 'IP' stand for in an IP address?
trivia.a: Internet Protocol — the address that identifies your device on a network.
Someone else's computers, accessed over the internet, where your files and apps live.

trivia.q: What does 'defragment' mean for a hard drive?
trivia.a: Reordering scattered file pieces so they sit contiguously again, speeding up reads on an HDD.
A network of hijacked devices controlled together, often used to flood websites with traffic.
Securely control another computer over a network from the command line.
It keeps frequently used data close to the CPU so fetches are fast.
Graphical User Interface — windows, icons, and a mouse instead of typed commands.
Any software built to harm, hijack, or spy — viruses, trojans, and ransomware are all malware.
Automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining a network.
Low-level software baked into a device that tells its hardware how to boot and behave.
Application Programming Interface — a contract that lets two programs talk to each other.
The delay before data starts moving — low latency means snappy, high latency means laggy.
JavaScript Object Notation — a lightweight text format for exchanging data.
A square barcode a phone camera reads to open a link or info instantly.
Translates a name like onyxpc.us into the IP address computers actually route to.
Phishing is a mass scam; spear phishing is the same trick aimed at one specific person.
Uniform Resource Locator — the address of a page or file on the web.
When a chip slows itself down to avoid overheating, trading speed for safety.
Redundant Array of Independent Disks — combining drives for speed or backup.
Physical designs (like Raspberry Pi) published so anyone can study, modify, and build them.
The encrypted channel between your browser and a site, shown by the padlock icon.
The smallest dot of light on a screen; millions of them make up an image.
How much data can move through a connection at once — the width of the pipe.
Using disk space as extra RAM when physical memory runs low.
To translate human-written code into machine code the CPU can run.
A background process that quietly handles printing, updates, or network tasks.
Whether a device is reachable on the network and how long the round trip takes.
